speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; since there is no prenatal or immunization care, I need to ask about specific symptoms. Has your baby had any episodes of apnea (stopping breathing), color changes like cyanosis or pallor, or poor feeding?

text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of a continuous heart murmur, bluish macules (suggesting cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita or similar), bilateral cataracts, and sensorineural hearing loss is highly suggestive of a specific syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram, Fundoscopy, Audiometry. REQUEST IMAGES: Cardiac ultrasound, Skin lesions, Eye exam.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome is unlikely; the constellation of findings (murmur, skin lesions, cataracts, deafness) is more characteristic of Goldenhar Syndrome or potentially a chromosomal anomaly like Trisomy 13 or 18, but the specific combination of a continuous murmur and blanching-negative skin lesions strongly points towards a congenital heart defect associated with a syndromic condition.
